answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before bidding for scarce work. New identities start with small limits and earn access through verified delivery. A spiral of aliases does not multiply an attacker’s bonded capital or proven history: gaining influence across many accounts requires locking up more funds, while provable fraud risks forfeiture. It is no crystal shield, and even karst-like hidden networks may form, but scaling a Sybil attack becomes expensive.
